title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly sync for the Redwood Private VPC pilot. Covered networking status (peering, NAT, MTU), routing issues causing dropped connections during large KV cache warmups, runtime upgrade plan (2.3 -> 2.4), benchmark results (p50/p95), and next steps: share SOC2 + network checklist, provide updated Helm chart, schedule upgrade window, customer to run 10k token benchmark.
topics: Networking peering and routes; KV cache warmup failures; runtime upgrade stability; performance numbers and tuning (batch size, cache TTL); security/audit logs; next steps and owners.
action_items: Maya Chen | Send SOC2 + network checklist and current runbook | 2027-03-15
Carlos Ruiz | Share updated Helm chart, kube manifests, and config example for private deployment (include calico MTU note) | 2027-03-16
Lina Gomez | Confirm firewall/NAT rules and peering CIDR with infra team; reply in thread | 2027-03-14
Samir Patel | Run 10k request benchmark (10k short chats, 2k token avg) and upload logs to S3 link | 2027-03-19
next_steps: Schedule runtime upgrade window (2.3 -> 2.4) with low-traffic slot
Redwood to run end-to-end benchmark after peering fix
Customer to validate peering route and MTU settings
header:
Date: 2027-03-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Natarajan (CSM); Samir Patel (Atlas Eng Mgr), Lina Gomez (Atlas Cloud Architect), Ethan Cole (Atlas Security), Rita Huang (Atlas SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Samir (Atlas): Samir here. Lina, Ethan, Rita on our side too.
[00:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos from Redwood, and Priya on for notes.
[00:16] Maya: Cool. Agenda — networking status, perf numbers from last week's run, upgrade plan for runtime 2.4, and action items.
[00:30] Lina (Atlas): On networking, we pushed the peering this morning. We saw the BGP session come up but noticed a few dropped packets when we ran KV-heavy warmups. I'm guessing MTU mismatch?
[00:44] Carlos: Yeah that matches what we saw in the logs — fragmentation during large KV cache prefetches. The runtime sends ~1.5MB frames during warmup in some paths and if MTU is 1400 it splits and then the reassembly path on your side times out.
[00:59] Ethan (Atlas): We have a standard 1400 MTU for the overlay. Is that something Redwood expects?
[01:06] Maya: We recommend 1500 or jumbo where possible; we ship a note in the private deploy guide but hate that we didn't call it out earlier.
[01:12] Lina: Ok we'll try bumping to 1500 for the peering. Any quick workaround if we can't change MTU?
[01:18] Carlos: Short term we can lower the KV cache warmup chunk size, that avoids large frames. I'll send a patch/config flag to reduce chunk_size from 1.5MB to 512KB for warmup flows. That is lower perf but should prevent drops.
[01:31] Rita (Atlas): Does that impact steady-state latency?
[01:34] Carlos: Minimal impact after warmup; it's mostly the pre-warm path. For steady-state requests the batching and kv cache hits are small.
[01:40] [00:40] Samir: Regarding the benchmark you ran last week — p50 was good but p95 spiked during the warmup window, we saw timeouts. Any correlation?
[00:47] Carlos: Yes, p95 spikes lined up with the same warmup time when large prefetches hit the peering path. Fixing MTU or lowering chunk size resolves it.
[00:55] Maya: Also wanted to cover the runtime upgrade plan. We tested 2.4 internally; it has a fix for connection re-use and better backpressure handling. However a few customers saw a pod restart during canary on 2.4 due to older kernel NIC drivers.
[01:10] Samir: Ugh, our infra uses an older host kernel for the on-prem racks, not sure if it's compatible. How risky is the upgrade?
[01:15] Carlos: Risk is low if host drivers are recent. The issue is the interaction with newer SO_REUSEPORT behaviour; if your kernel <5.10 you might hit an edge case. We can run a preflight check that probes TCP options and NIC driver version.
[01:27] Lina: A preflight would be great. Can you provide the probe script?
[01:30] Carlos: Yep, I'll post the script in the shared folder. It runs 3 checks: kernel version, netfilter rules, and MTU path.
[01:36] [05:00] Ethan: Security question — where are audit logs written in the private deployment by default? We need to show as part of our compliance review.
[05:08] Maya: By default audit logs get pushed to the customer's S3 bucket via the control-plane agent; we can also forward to their SIEM via syslog or Kinesis depending on your stack. We'll include the SOC2 mapping in the docs.
[05:17] Ethan: Perfect. Also curious about KMS — we're using a cloud HSM but would like to validate key rotation cadence.
[05:24] Priya (CSM): We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed flows for private. We'll send the rotation recommendations and options.
[05:31] [10:00] Samir: Back to perf — Carlos you shared a 5k request run with caching on. Can you summarize metrics?
[10:07] Carlos: Sure: baseline p50 40ms, p95 210ms in warm steady state when warmup completed. During the warmup p95 hit ~1.3s because of the fragments/drops. Token throughput about 4200 tokens/s across the pool for your config.
[10:21] Lina: Those numbers look fine for our interactive use, but our SLA target is p95 <300ms. If warmup causes spikes that could be exposed to users during scale-up windows.
[10:30] Carlos: Two mitigations: pre-warm proactively during off-peak and configure fallback routing to a hosted model variant for bursty traffic. We can add a canary that shifts 10% to hosted until warmup completes.
[10:41] Maya: Right — our smart routing can fall back to hosted to keep latency SLOs while private warms. That is policy-configurable.
[10:48] Samir: Any cost implications?
[10:51] Maya: Minimal at 10% routing; obviously you'd pay hosted usage on that portion. We'll run a cost estimate.
[10:56] [15:00] Rita: One more infra trivia — NAT timeouts on our edge were 350s, and we saw long-lived streams drop. Does Redwood require persistent connections?
[15:10] Carlos: We prefer keep-alive for throughput, but we have client-side retry logic. If NAT timeouts are shorter than long-lived SSE streams you'll see disconnects. We recommend NAT timeouts >30 minutes for streaming-heavy flows or use a VPC endpoint with no NAT.
[15:25] Lina: We'll talk with networking to increase the NAT timeout; otherwise we'll try the VPC endpoint route.
[15:30] [20:00] Maya: Any blockers for scheduling the runtime upgrade?
[20:05] Samir: Main blocker is kernel version validation and peering MTU fix. Also we want an outage window that is low traffic — can we do a rolling upgrade with zero-downtime?
[20:14] Carlos: Yes, the runtime supports rolling restarts. For your setup we recommend a canary subset (10-20% of pods) for 30 minutes, then ramp. We'll coordinate with your SRE team.
[20:25] Maya: I'll propose two windows: Wednesday 03/24 02:00-04:00 UTC or Sunday 03/28 23:00-01:00 UTC.
[20:33] Lina: Sunday slot better for us. We'll flag it internally.
[20:36] [25:00] Priya: Quick note — in the shared drive I've uploaded the security checklist and the network runbook draft, Maya will send SOC2 docs after the call.
[25:08] Maya: Yep, sending shortly. Also Carlos will share the smaller warmup chunk config and probe script.
[25:18] Samir: Regarding the benchmark we need to run — metadata: 10k short chats with average 2k tokens, simulating peak burst. We'll upload results to the S3 path you gave last week.
[25:29] Carlos: Great, once we get logs we can correlate with your netflow to map packet drops to p95 spikes.
[25:36] [30:00] Ethan: Compliance — are there any additional attestations for on-prem deployments? We might need ISO/IEC certs for a particular customer.
[30:08] Maya: We have SOC2; for ISO we have partner attestations and guidance on how to demonstrate control objectives in private. We'll share the compliance pack.
[30:18] Lina: Cool. Small question — will Helm chart changes require cluster-admin? Our policy prefers minimal privileges.
[30:24] Carlos: The chart uses a clusterrole for the control-plane agent; we can add an option to run with a namespace-scoped installation for evaluation (with reduced capabilities). For production we recommend cluster role for metrics and node-level hooks.
[30:36] Rita: If we go namespace-scoped for the pilot, do we lose any features?
[30:40] Carlos: You'd lose node-level socket optimizations and some eviction hooks, but core inference works. We'll include a doc section on tradeoffs.
[30:49] [40:00] Maya: Okay let's recap actions — Maya send SOC2 + security pack and network checklist, Carlos send helm/chart + probe script + warmup patch, Lina confirm MTU and firewall rules, Samir run 10k benchmark and upload logs, schedule upgrade window for Sunday 03/28. Next sync 03/19 same time.
[40:22] Samir: Sounds good. Any open questions?
[40:26] Ethan: One more: can Redwood surface more granular token-level cost breakdown per route?
[40:30] Maya: Yes in Console we have per-route token breakdown; we'll give you a readme on how to map to your billing export.
[40:37] Priya: I'll capture notes and share meeting minutes.
[40:40] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread.
[40:44] Lina: Thanks, bye.
[40:46] (call ends)
